assertions.assert: Each element takes exactly its declared attributes, the required ones present, and no content, and the namespace has no other element: a malformed element raises error.execution and assigns nothing (its schema, package/processing.xsd, rejects it before any run under scx validate).

<processing:model_facing_schema> drops $schema, title and examples at every schema level, keeping property names; over the bound it drops every description, and still over it writes [], with overlocation true exactly when it wrote [].

<processing:collect_offered_events> writes the document's own choices tagged with its _sessionid, then each offer's choices and the focused device's events (schema {type: object}, tagged with its id) in name order, each offer's tagged with <_sessionid>.<invoke id>, made model-facing, with its size and whether it is over the bound.

<processing:send> writes the dispatch tool as one schema: its description as the root description and its parameters {events: [anyOf one branch per offered event]} with the tool's fixed descriptions and examples, and max as the events' maxItems; each branch {event, data, reason?, target?} has event a one-value enum, data the choice's schema without $schema (an empty object for none, wrapped as value for a non-object), required only when the schema requires a field, the schema's description else the event name, and target, required, a sorted enum of the offering targets when one has a target; nothing is normalized for strict decoding.

<processing:selection_confidence> writes the least of the selections' confidences, each normalized (a number in (0, 1] scaled to 0-100, rounded half to even, clamped to 0-100), leaving out a selection whose confidence is not a number, and null when none is left.
A location or expression that does not hold what the element reads raises error.execution and assigns nothing.
